sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 359.1 ± 8.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: PMC13266011 (L2): receptor used as membrane-anchored, surface-displayed construct for MRGPRX2 signaling studies; surface display confirmed. PMC9150435 (L1): full-length receptor purified from insect-cell membranes for structural (cryo-EM) studies, confirming membrane integration.
sites.rationale: MRGPRX2 is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; the N-terminus (residues 1–31, EC1) is the sole extracellular terminus, and the C-terminus (residues 284–330, IC4) is intracellular. Both L1 and L2/L3 describe constructs in which an exogenous HAss drives a FLAG tag to the extracellular N-terminus; after HAss cleavage the FLAG sits immediately before residue M1, giving insert_after_residue = 0. No residue number is named in either quote, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists, so the junction is topology-derived. The tag position is 31 residues from TM1 (starts at 32), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. Full-length human MRGPRX2 expressed as HAss-FLAG-MRGPRX2 in pcDNA3.1 in mammalian cells (PMC13266011; L2/L3); independently replicated as HAss-FLAG-His10-TEV-MRGPRX2 in pFastBac1 for insect-cell expression (PMC9150435; L1). In both constructs an exogenous HA signal peptide drives the FLAG tag to the extracellular face; the HAss is cleaved post-translationally, leaving FLAG displayed at the receptor N-terminus.

sources.claim: WT human MRGPRX2 with an N-terminal hemagglutinin signal sequence (“HAss”) followed by a FLAG tag was PCR amplified from the MRGPRX2 TANGO plasmid ( 73 ) (Addgene plasmid 66440), adding a stop codon following the MRGPRX2 coding sequence.

literature_notes: L4 (GeneCopoeia commercial plasmid, pReceiver-MO6) was excluded because the tag position is unstated — the rules explicitly disqualify commercial plasmids with no pinned insert site. L5 (PMC9273857) reports surface vs. total expression of an HA-tagged MRGPRX2 but names no residue and does not describe the construct design; it adds no independent position information and was not used. L6 (PMC13035742) describes a MRGPRX2-HA construct (C-terminal HA by naming convention) used for immunoprecipitation and phosphorylation studies; the C-terminus falls in IC4 (residues 284–330, intracellular) and is therefore not a surface tag site — recorded in other_positions. L1 and L2/L3 both support the same N-terminal prepend junction; a single site is reported (ranked by best functional evidence, L2) rather than two, because both papers pin the identical junction.

literature_other_positions.note: MRGPRX2-HA construct used for immunoprecipitation and phospho-Ser327/Ser328 detection; the C-terminus (IC4, residues 284–330) is intracellular, so this HA tag is cytoplasmic and not a surface tag site.
